title: Degreewise split extension by shifted free complexes is K-projective
statement: Let A be a commutative ring in universe u, and K and L be cochain complexes of A-modules with carriers in max(u,v) [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Let f : K → L be a chain map. Suppose K is K-projective, every component f in degree k has an A-linear left inverse, and the cokernel complex of f is isomorphic to a coproduct of complexes concentrated in degrees degree(i), with rank-one free module ULift^v A in those degrees, indexed by I in Type max(u,v). Then L is K-projective. No boundedness of K, L, or degree(i) is assumed.

proof.text: The componentwise left inverses make f monic and give a degreewise split short exact sequence 0 → K → L → Q → 0, where Q is the cokernel of f. Such an admissible exact sequence gives a distinguished triangle in the homotopy category, as in Stacks Tags 09KL and 09KJ.

For an acyclic N, a map from a rank-one free single complex in degree d is determined by a cycle z in N in degree d. Choose a primitive y in degree d - 1 using acyclicity. Sending the free generator to y gives a null homotopy. The same construction works for shifts of N and for every generator of a coproduct. The coproduct universal property assembles the homotopies; no boundedness of the degrees is needed. Transfer this vanishing to Q along the hypothesis isomorphism.

Apply Hom(-, N) to the admissible exact sequence triangle. The Hom groups for Q and K vanish, by the preceding step and K-projectivity respectively. Exactness forces the Hom group for L to vanish. Vanishing in the homotopy category gives a null homotopy for every chain map L → N, which is K-projectivity.

mathlib_searches.query: A degreewise split extension of a K-projective complex by a sum of shifts of free modules is K-projective
A zero cochain complex is K-projective; extensions by coproducts of shifted free modules are K-projective
mathlib_searches.results: CochainComplex.isKProjective_of_projective; isKProjective_iff_leftOrthogonal; projective resolution special cases. None handles arbitrary unbounded coproducts and extensions.

mathlib_searches.query: IsKProjective|isKProjective; degreewiseSplit; coproduct|Coproduct in Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/HomotopyCategory and the two project roots
mathlib_searches.results: Mathlib has bounded-above K-projectivity and degreewise-split triangles, but no split-extension K-projectivity theorem. The project contains only the filtered-free stage/telescope statements and bounded projective applications.

from.place: Derived base change resolving models: finite-stage induction in the filtered-free K-projectivity argument.

theorem isKProjective_of_filtered_free_step {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    {K L : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} A) ℤ}
    (f : K ⟶ L) (hprev : K.IsKProjective)
    (hsplit : ∀ k : ℤ, ∃ r : L.X k ⟶ K.X k,
      f.f k ≫ r = 𝟙 (K.X k))
    (hquot : ∃ (I : Type (max u v)) (degree : I → ℤ),
      Nonempty (cokernel f ≅ ∐ (fun i : I ↦
        (HomologicalComplex.single (ModuleCat.{max u v} A) (.up ℤ) (degree i)).obj
          (ModuleCat.of A (ULift.{v} A))))) :
    L.IsKProjective
